abstract.para: Learn how to configure &minimalvm; images using interactive &jeosfirstboot;.

topic.para: By default, if you boot the virtual machine without providing an automated configuration method (such as &combustion; or cloud-init), the system launches &jeosfirstboot;. To deploy the image interactively, manually complete this text-based wizard on the system console. Deploying involves two tasks:

listitem.para: Start the virtual machine on your platform.
Configure the system on the first boot with &jeosfirstboot;.

note.title: Exception for &zseries;
note.para: On &s390x; flavors targeting z/VM (such as DASD and FCP), the &jeosfirstboot; wizard is not supported due to terminal limitations. On these images, systemd-firstboot is used instead.

topic.para: Because starting a virtual machine varies wildly by platform, the exact procedure depends on your hypervisor. For Hyper-V and VMware images, use their management tools to create the virtual machine.

section.title: Starting a &kvm; virtual machine
section.para: For kvm-and-xen images, you can start the virtual machine directly by using &qemu; or virt-install.

section.title: Configuring a system with &jeosfirstboot;
section.para: &jeosfirstboot; is a text-based wizard that runs on the first boot and collects the basic settings. It appears on the console of the virtual machine, whichever platform you started it on.

step.para: Read and accept the license agreement. You cannot proceed without accepting it.
Optionally, enroll keys for SSH access and create additional user accounts.
After the first boot, register the system. For more information see . If you are only testing the image, you can skip registration.
